title: Master Keaton
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Taichi Hiraga Keaton, son of a Japanese zoologist and an English noblewoman, is an archaeology lecturer and insurance investigator for Lloyd's who once served in the SAS. Episodic cases take him across Europe and beyond, where he uses knowledge and survival skills more than force.
life_message: It holds up compassion, knowledge and quiet competence as the way to resolve conflict and help people.

content.note: Thieves, assassins, bombs and deaths, though the review says action is understated (VIZ blurb; MU Bombs, Death; ANN review).
Keaton saves a woman from prostitution in one story (ANN review).
Drug dealing appears as a real-world issue (ANN review).

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Keaton resolves situations through insight rather than personal retaliation (ANN review).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Works within Lloyd's and university structures while acting independently.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Helps strangers in each case; also a father (MU Divorced Protagonist).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: A half-noble hero who treats people of all classes alike (to verify).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Archaeology and investigative reason drive the stories.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Survival skills matter, but he pursues his scholarly dream (to verify).

folkways.japan: A Japanese seinen series with a half-Japanese, half-English hero set mainly in 1980s Europe; Japanese norms appear mainly in his modesty and work ethic.

delivery.evidence: ANN reviewer repeatedly describes the themes as 'subtly' expressed, prioritizing character motivation.
delivery.note: Episodic cases let values emerge through Keaton's choices rather than speeches.

winners_losers: Keaton and the people he helps; criminals and exploiters lose. Compassion and knowledge get sympathy.
to_verify: ANN review covers volume 1 only; later arcs may include more war and terrorism content.
VIZ English edition is 12 omnibus volumes.
